recommendation: Use Hong Kong and Gothenburg as the main evaluated precedents. The Indonesian case is an optional, clearly labelled rural participation precedent, not a comparable border city.
cross_case_guardrails: These are evaluated interventions, not evidence that their effects will transfer to Hong Kong–Shenzhen.
Keep observed results separate from proposed local pilots. None tests HK–Shenzhen border delays, cross-border entitlement portability, or a change in service eligibility.
Individual adaptation, employment, service use, social connection, and voice are distinct outcomes. Do not label improvement in one as proof of integration in all four lenses.

cases.project: FAMILY Project / International Social Service Hong Kong Branch: combined settlement information and wellbeing support
cases.dates: Fieldwork April 2012–July 2013; published in Behavior Therapy, 2022.
lenses: connection/cohesion: individual adaptation, not measured community cohesion
cases.intervention: Social workers delivered four weekly 2.5-hour sessions combining information on education, community resources, health care, employment and housing with self-efficacy, positive thinking, altruism and goal-setting activities.
cases.design: Cluster randomized trial of 251 recent mainland Chinese family-reunion immigrants: information-only n=84; wellbeing-only n=80; combined n=87. All three arms were active interventions.
cases.measured_outcome: From immediately after the intervention to six months, the combined arm had better sustained knowledge and adaptation-difficulty trajectories than information alone, and better resilience and mental-health trajectories than wellbeing alone.
cases.denominator_and_time: 251 randomized, not necessarily 251 completing follow-up. Arms 84/80/87; assessments through six months. A follow-up completer denominator and a simple interpretable effect magnitude were not verified; do not invent a percentage improvement.
cases.strongest_justified_claim: Combining practical orientation and psychological support performed better on selected sustained adaptation measures than delivering either component alone in this study.
cases.limits: Older, selected newcomer sample; no untreated control. Outcomes do not demonstrate increased completed service use, reduced border friction, or stronger community cohesion.
cases.plausible_hksz_response_inference: Test an assisted navigation service for a defined cross-border resident group: one named navigator, a practical task such as completing an appointment or school enquiry, and optional peer support. Measure successful task completion, time/cost, unresolved eligibility problems and follow-up wellbeing separately. The navigator and cross-border components are proposed adaptations, not trial-proven mechanisms.
cases.suggested_site_copy: Hong Kong tested practical settlement information together with wellbeing support. In a randomized study of 251 mainland newcomers, the combined programme showed better sustained adaptation on selected measures over six months. A local pilot should check whether people can actually complete the service task, as well as whether they feel more supported.

cases.dates: Programme launched 2016; randomized cohort April 2017; initial programme ended Q1 2018. Follow-up through Q4 2021; long-run evaluation published December 2023.
cases.intervention: Three months of intensive Swedish, six months of supervised work practice, then professional job-search help; coordinated by the employment service, city and municipal housing group.
cases.design: 140 low-educated newly arrived refugees randomized 70/70. Of 70 offered the programme, 44 started. Intention-to-treat comparisons retain all 70 offered, rather than comparing only participants with controls.
cases.measured_outcome: The original two-year evaluation reported roughly 30% employed per month in the offered group versus 15% in usual services during the year after the programme. A later evaluation using earnings-based employment measures found an approximately 15-percentage-point advantage lasting about three years; controls caught up by the end of follow-up.
cases.denominator_and_time: Original result: 70 assigned per arm; monthly employment, second year after April 2017 randomization. Later measure: positive earnings from unsubsidized work or a New Start Job during a month, observed through Q4 2021. Do not splice the two outcome definitions into one chart.
cases.strongest_justified_claim: The complete support bundle accelerated entry into employment in this sample.
cases.limits: Small, single-city refugee sample. The bundle cannot identify which component caused the gain. Long-run results did not establish broader social integration; gender differences and different job opportunities matter.
cases.plausible_hksz_response_inference: Pilot an employer-linked pathway for one defined occupation: role-specific skills/language, supervised placement and a named caseworker. Verify work authorization and credential requirements before referral. Track sustained work, earnings, placement quality and participation barriers separately from belonging.
cases.suggested_site_copy: Gothenburg joined language learning to supervised work practice and job-search support. A 140-person randomized trial found faster entry into employment, with an advantage lasting around three years. Broader integration did not automatically follow, so work and belonging need separate measures.

cases.place: 49 rural villages in East Java, North Sumatra and Southeast Sulawesi, Indonesia
cases.dates: Fieldwork September 2005–January 2006; published in American Political Science Review, 2010.
cases.intervention: 17 villages were assigned direct voting on local infrastructure proposals; 32 used representative meetings. Adults voted on the general proposal; women also selected a women’s proposal.
cases.design: Village-level randomized field experiment; intention-to-treat analysis. The intervention changed project selection, not initial proposal generation or final inter-village funding decisions.
cases.measured_outcome: Nearly 80% turnout, around 20 times meeting participation, with higher measured satisfaction and project knowledge. The mix of projects changed little. Women's projects were more likely to be located in the poorest hamlet.
cases.denominator_and_time: 49 randomized villages, split 17/32. The paper's turnout denominator uses eligible voters from the previous village-head election as a proxy for eligible project voters. Satisfaction was surveyed after selection, not after years of completed-project use.
cases.strongest_justified_claim: Making a concrete project choice broadly accessible can increase participation and perceived legitimacy even when the selected project mix changes little.
cases.limits: Rural, non-migrant setting; no border-city transfer established. Voting at one stage does not establish control over agenda-setting, spending or implementation. Do not describe this as proof of reduced inequality or better completed infrastructure.
cases.plausible_hksz_response_inference: For a small, clearly bounded neighbourhood-service budget, test accessible resident choice among feasible improvements and publish how the selected option affects delivery. Include shift workers and cross-border residents in designing the choices. Measure who participates, whose suggestions reach the ballot, and whether promised changes happen.
cases.suggested_site_copy: In 49 Indonesian villages, changing infrastructure-project selection from meetings to a public vote brought far more residents into the decision and raised satisfaction. It also exposed a limit: choosing from a list is only one part of having a voice. This is a rural participation precedent, not a tested HK–Shenzhen solution.

implementation_guidance: A compact card can use: what was tried; what changed; how it was tested; what this does not show; a local idea to test.
Avoid a big 'success rate' number for the Hong Kong case: allocation and follow-up duration are verified, but a plain percentage effect is not.
For a strict city-only edit, omit the Indonesian case and say local voice remains a question requiring a bounded pilot, rather than stretching the two city trials.
Current policy or eligibility facts in any proposed HK–Shenzhen service must be verified independently at the point of design.
